chapter: Hightower: New Orleans parades and early players
title: Buddy Bolden and the balloon advertisement at Lincoln Park
summary: He recalls Bolden playing from a wagon to advertise Lincoln Park, with a balloon ascension, and breaking down.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Do you remember anything about Bolden? And I'm going to stop talking to you. I'm not going to make you talk anymore. If you can just tell a little bit about Bolden if you remember when you heard him.

Just enough to know that about, I don't know how long it was, but just about the time I got, I wasn't old enough to play then, see. Yeah. I played at a place called the Lincoln Park. That's around Carlton Avenue. Yeah. It used to have Buddy Bolden, used to go up in a balloon. Man used to go up in a balloon because it was a parish. Buddy Barclay that was.
Buddy Barclay, that's what it was.
Yeah. Buddy Barclay, that's what it was.
I heard it. I never saw it, but I heard it.

Yeah. Well, he was playing an advertisement for that Lincoln Park, for that Sunday, at Melkameen and Drys. Everybody, what was that, the market? It used to be the market. No, the old Drys market. It's still there. It's still there? Yeah, well, there's all Melkameen. Well, he blew his brains out right there.
Just playing an advertisement for the Lincoln Park. In a puncture wagon.
